title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page continues a computation in the sequel to La Longue Marche (manuscript pp. 705–705'). The setting appears to be genus-1 Teichmüller/Galois theory with one puncture. Π_0 is presumably the fundamental group of a once-punctured torus, free on two generators. 𝔖_0 is a group of automorphisms containing Π_0, and H^+ = 𝔖_0/Π_0 is the oriented outer automorphism group. It has the presentation <ρ,σ | ρ^3=σ^2=ω, ω central of order 2>, so H^+ ≅ SL_2(Z), with ω = −1. 𝔖^+ is the quotient of 𝔖_0 by the derived subgroup of Π_0, so 𝔖^+ is an extension of H^+ by M = Π_0^{ab} ≅ Z^2 (in the notes K ≅ Z^2). Everything is done for locally constant group schemes over a base S_0 or S, with roots of unity μ and Φ_12^* in the background.

On the previous page, a candidate splitting is written as ρ' = ξρ, σ' = ησ with ξ, η sections of M. Since ω is central in H^+ and acts trivially on M, any splitting must send ω to ω (relation (268)). The relations ρ'^3 = σ'^2 = ω then reduce to two conditions: (1+ρ_M+ρ_M^2)ξ = 0 and (1+σ_M)η = 0. The remaining relation σ'(ρ') = ρ'^{-1} gives equation (249), made explicit in (250).

Conclusion on this page:
- A splitting exists over some S_0-scheme Z. This is equivalent to splitting the discrete extension of H^+ by M.
- The splittings form a torsor under K ≅ Z^2, identified with M (254).
- M acts on the set of splittings by conjugation, simply transitively.

Proposition (over an arbitrary base S):
- The extension of H^+ by M (as group schemes) is split.
- Any two splittings are conjugate by a unique section of M.
- Passing to the quotient by F_𝔖 gives a bijection between splittings of 𝔖^+ → H^+ and splittings of 𝔖^+/F_𝔖 → H^+/F_{H^+} ≅ 𝔖_3.

In modern terms, the first two points say H^1(SL_2(Z), Z^2) = 0 and (Z^2)^{SL_2(Z)} = 0. The splitting of Z^2 ⋊ SL_2(Z) is then unique up to a unique conjugation, and this rigidity can be detected at a finite level with quotient S_3 ≅ SL_2(F_2). The next page uses this to compute centralizers of the lifted subgroups H(ρ',σ') inside G_{ρ,σ}.
errors: No mathematical error is visible. The claim checks: by Mayer–Vietoris for SL_2(Z) = Z/4 *_{Z/2} Z/6 with M = Z^2, we have M^{Z/2} = 0 because −1 acts as −1. H^1(Z/6, M) = 0 because det(1−ρ) = 1 for an element of order 6. H^1(Z/4, M) = Z/2 injects into H^1(Z/2, M) = M/2M. Hence H^1 = 0 and M^G = 0, which gives existence, uniqueness up to conjugacy, and uniqueness of the conjugating element.

Gap: the precise definition of F_𝔖 / F_{H^+} (a finite-index normal subgroup with quotient S_3) is not on this page. The bijection statement therefore cannot be fully checked here; it is plausible provided F_𝔖 ∩ M is handled compatibly.

ideas.what: Extension of SL_2(Z) (= oriented Out of the free group F_2) by Z^2 = F_2^{ab} splits, with splittings forming an M-torsor under conjugation
ideas.modern_name: H^1(SL_2(Z), Z^2) = 0 and H^0 = 0; uniqueness of splitting of Z^2 ⋊ SL_2(Z)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (group cohomology of SL_2(Z) via the amalgam Z/4 *_{Z/2} Z/6)

ideas.what: Doing the same computation for locally constant group schemes over an arithmetic base (S_0 with μ, Φ_12^*), i.e. a scheme-theoretic version of the genus-1 Teichmüller group with ρ, σ of orders 3 and 2
ideas.modern_name: Arithmetic genus-1 (1,1) Teichmüller tower / elliptic modular group as group scheme
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Esquisse), later Nakamura, Lochak–Schneps et al. for profinite/GT versions
ideas.where_published: Possibly La Longue Marche (1981); unsure about this precise statement

ideas.what: Reducing splittings to a finite quotient H^+/F ≅ S_3
ideas.modern_name: Rigidity of splittings detected at level 2 (SL_2(Z) → SL_2(F_2) ≅ S_3)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a careful but routine group-cohomology verification inside the genus-1 Teichmüller computations of the Longue Marche sequel. The vanishing of H^1(SL_2(Z), Z^2) and the resulting rigidity of splittings are standard. Nothing here appears new to specialists.
transcription_corrections: 'passage au quotient par Fa' should read 'par F_𝔖' (F with subscript 𝔖), matching '𝔖^+/F_𝔖' in the last line.
'il existe une scindage sur un S_0-schéma Z' – likely 'il existe un scindage' (Grothendieck writes 'des scindages').
'correspondant à l'opération de M sur le scindage des scindages' likely reads 'sur l'ensemble des scindages, par conjugaison'.
'une torseur sous K' should read 'un torseur sous K'.
Line 'et en fait K ... une sous[?]' likely reads 'et en fait K est un sous-[groupe]... on a M ≃ K (254)', followed by 'd'où M ≃ K' (underlined).
